newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom same-store sales up 5 pct in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom same-store sales up 5 pct in Q2.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc said Monday that comparable-store sales jumped 5 percent in its fiscal second quarter and have risen 3.1 percent for the year to date.
Nordstrom, which unlike most retailers does not report monthly sales figures, said comparable-store sales rose 3.4 percent in May, 1.5 percent in June and 9.3 percent in July.
Comparable-store or same-store sales figures, which exclude new stores and expansions, are watched closely by analysts and investors as a sign of underlying business trends.
"We are encouraged by an increase in sales, better expense control and gross margin improvements," Nordstrom Chairman John Whitacre said in a statement.
He said the comparable-store sales in the quarter ending July 31 were boosted by strong performance throughout the chain during its recent annual anniversary sale.
Nordstrom also said sales rose 38 percent in its catalog division.

Nordstrom said expenses in the current third quarter would be higher than in the year-ago period due to the opening of a catalog fulfillment center in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, and three new full-line stores -- two on New York's Long Island and one in Cleveland.
